# design-diff

> design-diff shows what a pull request does to a Python codebase's architecture:
> which classes were added, removed, or modified; which properties and methods
> changed inside each class; and which dependencies (inheritance, composition)
> grew or shrank between classes. Output is a GitHub-diff-style picture (a
> self-contained SVG, no external dependencies) embedded in the PR comment, or
> machine-readable JSON for AI reviewers.
> Install: `uv add design-diff` (or `pip install design-diff`).
> CLI: `design-diff diff <base_ref> <head_ref> --package <pkg> --format svg|json|mermaid`
> (`svg` is the default image format; `json` is for programmatic/LLM consumption).
> GitHub Action: add one workflow file and every same-repo pull request gets an
> automatic, upserted comment (see "Quick start (GitHub Action)" in README).
> Requires type annotations to detect dependencies. Executes the analyzed code
> via import — only run against trusted (same-repo) code.

## Capabilities

- Diffs two git refs (branches, tags, or commits) and detects: added/removed/
  modified classes; added/removed/changed properties and methods within each
  class; added/removed inheritance and composition edges between classes.
- `--format svg` (default): a self-contained, GitHub-diff-style SVG rendered
  directly by design-diff (no Mermaid, no external renderer, no network
  fetch). Added members render as green rows with a `+` gutter, removed
  members as red rows with strikethrough, changed members as a yellow
  "old signature → new signature" row; added/removed edges as labeled
  green/red-dashed lines.
- `--format json`: a self-contained payload — `summary`, per-class
  `attributes`/`methods` diffs, `relations`, a `mermaid` field with an
  equivalent classDiagram rendering, and a `warnings` array. Designed to be
  dropped straight into an LLM reviewer's context.
- `--format mermaid`: plain Mermaid `classDiagram` text (also embedded as a
  `<details>` fallback inside the GitHub Action's PR comment).
- GitHub Action posts one comment per PR and updates it in place on every
  push (no notification floods). It commits the SVG to a `design-diff-assets`
  branch and embeds it via a `raw.githubusercontent.com` URL, because GitHub
  sanitizes inline `<svg>`/data-URI `<img>` tags out of comment bodies.
- Silent by default: no comment when there is no structural change **and** no
  analysis warning. If a submodule failed to import, a comment is still
  posted with a warning, so "no changes" is never claimed for a partial
  analysis.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/t29mato/design-diff/main/README.md): what it does, quick start (Action and CLI), how it works, requirements & limitations
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/t29mato/design-diff/main/AGENTS.md): step-by-step runbook for an agent adopting design-diff into another repository, plus conventions for agents contributing to design-diff's own source
- [SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/t29mato/design-diff/main/SKILL.md): an agent skill that automates adoption (detects the package, writes the workflow file). Install with `npx skills add t29mato/design-diff` (any agent supported by [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)), or copy `.claude/skills/enable-design-diff/` into a repository's own `.claude/skills/` for direct Claude Code use.
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/t29mato/design-diff/main/CHANGELOG.md): version history
- [docs/design/architecture.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/t29mato/design-diff/main/docs/design/architecture.md): clean-architecture layering, domain model, diff algorithm, rendering policy, CI/security decisions and their rationale
- [docs/examples/](https://github.com/t29mato/design-diff/tree/main/docs/examples): real CLI output examples (unedited), including the JSON schema in practice

## Notes for AI reviewers

- `--format json` produces a self-contained JSON payload with a `mermaid` field
  containing an equivalent classDiagram rendering, so a reviewer can reproduce a
  human-readable diagram from the JSON alone. It also has a `warnings` array
  listing any submodule that failed to import during extraction (empty means
  the analysis covered the whole package).
- `has_changes: false` **and** `warnings: []` together mean no class-level
  structural change was detected and the analysis was complete; only then
  does the tool stay silent (no PR comment is posted). If `warnings` is
  non-empty, a comment is posted even with `has_changes: false`, so reviewers
  know the diff may be incomplete.
- The GitHub Action embeds the rendered SVG as an `<img>` in the PR comment
  (committed to an orphan `design-diff-assets` branch and referenced via a
  `raw.githubusercontent.com` URL, with the commit SHA rather than the branch
  name so the URL never serves stale cached content); the Mermaid block is
  kept as a `<details>` fallback in the same comment.

## Notes for AI agents adopting this tool

- See [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/t29mato/design-diff/main/AGENTS.md)
  for the full setup runbook: confirm the target is a Python project, determine
  the `--package` name, optionally verify locally, add the workflow file, and
  open a PR to confirm the comment appears.
- Fastest path: `npx skills add t29mato/design-diff` installs the
  `enable-design-diff` skill into any supported agent (Claude Code, Cursor,
  opencode, etc. — see [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)),
  then invoke it to detect the package and write the workflow file
  automatically.
